blocks.x: Care Management & Population Health runs on a structure your control owners can interrogate — the decision plane, the evidence plane and the governance plane stay separate in design and reconciled in operation.

items: When Member risk signals scattered is the pain, the baseline audit usually confirms it is structural, not personal — the fix is designed for the system, not the people.
Outreach operations manual is one of the pressures we hear first in estates like yours — the diagnostic puts a measured number on it before anything is promised.
We treat Program matching crude as a symptom with a cause — the diagnosis traces it to the decision or the contract that produces it.
Sensitive coordination data shows up in the first conversations with every team we meet in this space; the design gate assigns it an owner and a countermeasure.
Quality reporting burden is where programs like this usually start: unglamorous, measurable and worth more than the technology conversation it replaces.
Care-platform integration drag costs real money every quarter it goes unmeasured; the first two weeks of the engagement exist to price it honestly.
Data age treated like uptime — a budget, an owner and an alert when it slips.
Workloads land on the cheapest compute that still meets the latency budget.
Open table formats underneath everything we build, so your data never belongs to a vendor.
A single governance plane over tables, models and notebooks — access your auditors can replay.
Lab and trial data governed from instrument to submission — sample lineage intact.
Drug supply integrity monitored end to end — shortages predicted, not suffered.
Clinical context fetched under consent, in FHIR terms — decision support inside the clinician's flow.
Patient outreach orchestrated with consent and outcome measurement — engagement that respects the person.
Up 97–98.8% of tables inside their declared window per 1,000 patients, reported weekly against the signed baseline
Batch windows measured against the plan every run — the number reported is the observed one.
Spend per query attributed to the team that wrote it — the meter everyone can see.

One definition per metric, owned and versioned — the dashboard and the board pack cannot disagree.
Contracts enforced at the boundary — schema drift fails the pipeline loudly, in minutes.
